title: validate_set_emphasis/apply_set_emphasis retain the retired word while the command variant is Cmd_Set_Weights
detail: Audit scope column for this row says 'one union variant + comments', so proc names were not inventoried — but the rename commit edited these exact signatures in place, leaving the retired word in live core identifiers beside Cmd_Set_Weights. Oversight, not deliberate.
recommended_fix: Rename to validate_set_weights/apply_set_weights, matching the validate_set_lane/apply_set_lane convention; byte-neutral per the serialize.odin value-only proof, no golden fold.

title: qos_test.odin comments and expect-strings still call the Cmd_Set_Weights edit 'emphasis'
evidence:
core/qos_test.odin:132:
	// emphasis: unknown pipe / bad weights
core/qos_test.odin:178:
	// emphasis: the weight set applies directly (express_heavy's weights)
core/qos_test.odin:180:
	testing.expect(t, e == .None, "valid emphasis must apply clean")
core/qos_test.odin:182:
	testing.expectf(t, s.topology.gen > 1, "emphasis must bump gen (rule-1 rebuild trigger)")
core/qos_test.odin:238:
	// an emphasis edit MUST add exactly the weights section + change the hash
core/qos_test.odin:284:
	testing.expectf(t, len(cmds) == 3, "log must carry draw + emphasis + lane, got %d", len(cmds))
core/qos_test.odin:287:
		testing.expect(t, c.pipe == pipe && c.weights == [3]i32{4, 2, 1}, "emphasis record round-trips")
detail: The same rename commit (198f1f9) renamed every Cmd_Set_Emphasis{...} to Cmd_Set_Weights{...} and strain comments to congestion in this file, yet left 'emphasis' in live test comments describing the weight-set edit. Sweep residue in a file the sweep touched.
recommended_fix: Replace 'emphasis' with 'weights' in these comments and expect-strings (e.g. 'an emphasis edit' → 'a weights edit'); vocabulary-only, no behavior or golden impact.
